facts.text: Glacier Park Lodge, a National Historic Landmark, boasts a Great Hall with 60‑foot Douglas‑fir log pillars, making it one of Montana’s most architecturally striking hotels.
The East Glacier Park train depot, built in 1913, sits across from Glacier Park Lodge and was constructed by the Great Northern Railway during the same era.
East Glacier Park sits on the Blackfeet Nation and is less than ten miles from the Two Medicine entrance to Glacier National Park, blending cultural history with landscapes.
The town hosts Montana’s oldest grass‑greens golf course, a historic nine‑hole layout surrounded by landscaped gardens and mountain scenery.
